channel.title: Known bugs on Teaching materials with Hugo
channel.description: Recent content in Known bugs on Teaching materials with Hugo

item.title: (a) ref inside a Markdown link
item.description: A Markdown link whose address is a {{< ref >}} or {{< relref >}} shortcode points to a broken address.

item.title: (b) Pale slide text without colours.css
item.description: Slide text is pale grey on a pale slide when a site has no colours.css.

item.title: (c) Theme settings lost without _merge = 'deep'
item.description: A site’s own [outputs] or [markup] settings replace the theme’s, unless they say _merge = 'deep'.

item.title: (d) Copy buttons only for some languages
item.description: Only code blocks marked html, css, js, JavaScript, json, php or phtml get a “copy to clipboard” button.

item.title: (e) iframe with a page-relative address
item.description: {{< iframe src="demo/" >}} looks for demo/ at the top of the site, not next to the page.

item.title: (f) A slide as a page of its own is unstyled
item.description:
Fixed in: (not yet)

This page is the live example: it has type: slide, so it is shown on its own, outside a lecture. While the bug is there it looks bare, with no slide styling.

What is wrong: the theme’s layouts/slide/single.html only makes the <article class="slide">. Unlike a lecture it doesn’t load presentation.css or slide-types.css, so nothing styles it.

Workaround: don’t give slides pages of their own. Keep them in content/slides/ with build: render: never (see Advanced: site settings) and use them in a lecture.

item.title: (g) HTML files in content/ stop the build
item.description: With Hugo 0.162 or later, any .html file in content/ stops the build, unless the site allows it.

item.title: (h) Links starting with / or ../ lose the site's folder
item.description: On a site that lives in a folder (every GitHub Pages project site, such as …github.io/module-name/), links that start with / or ../ miss out the folder.

item.title: (i) HTML files next to an exercise aren't published
item.description: An iframe of an HTML file in an exercise’s own folder shows the site’s home page instead.
